newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary power workers say may strike over wages.
newsitem.headline: Hungary power workers say may strike over wages.

text.p: Hungarian trade unions said on Monday the government had created tensions over wages which may lead to strikes in the heavily western-owned energy sector.

The Electricity Industry Workers' Trade Union Association (VIDSZSZ) of Hungary staged protests for higher wages in Germany and Belgium on Friday -- in what the union leaders claimed was the first demonstration by eastern European employees at the headquarters of western European investors.
"I can blame the responsibility on the government and the Parliament," VDSZSZ Deputy President Gabor Major told Reuters.
"They should have created the guarantees, the regulation to ensure safe privatisation," he added. "In that case everybody would know his role, rights and obligations now."
Hungary was the first country in eastern Europe to sell large stakes in the energy sector to western investors one year ago, creating record privatisation revenue.
But the government disappointed the western investors by cancelling an energy price rise due in October and with a recent decision on energy price hikes for 1997, Major said.

The investors, claiming they would not receive the promised return, say they do not feel compelled to abide by previous agreements with the employees to keep up the real value of wages at the privatised firms in 1996, Major added.
The trade unions said employees would receive only a 19.5 percent back payment for 1996, while they were demanding 25 percent, which they say is in line with inflation.
Major said Friday's demonstrations and subsequent talks with representatives of Germany's RWE AG and Belgium's Tractebel, both investors in the Hungarian energy sector, have produced any results.
Major said VDSZSZ would decide on Friday if it should call a strike in the electricity sector, but workers of RWE's Matrai Power Station will hold another demonstration on Tuesday.
